full_judgment: 3. Defendant-respondent Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable and that the same was barred by limitation. Their definite case was that the suit land originally belonged to Anarullah Shaikh, Danesh Shaikh, Abdullah Shaikh and Wazeruddin Shaikh to the extent of 2 annas 8 gondas shares each and Fedullah Shaikh and Rahman Shaikh to the extent of 3 annas 4 gondas share each out of total area of 12.16 acres land under the then landlady Hemanta Kumari Debi. The said superior interest of the suit jote of Hemanta Kumari Debi was never sold to Anisuzzaman and another who had no rent receiving interest and as such they had no authority to file Rent Suit No. 59 of 1952 in the Court of Munsif, Khulna. The heirs of Anarullah Shaikh sold their interest to Binod Bihari Golder, who was in possession of the suit land. Hironmoy Roy also acquired some interest in the suit Jama and he transferred the same on 12.03.1952 to one Bashir. Further case of the defendants was that the plaintiffs had no authority to purchase the share of Binod Bihari and Hironmoy. Neither the right, title and interest of Binod Bihari nor that of Kalipada and others passed in the auction sale as claimed by the plaintiffs. While the suit land was in the khas possession of Binod Bihari, he paid rent to the Government and 5.06 acres land of CS Khatian No. 217 was mortgaged to the then Agricultural Development Bank, Khulna vide Loan Case No.745/61-62 dated 30.11.1962 from which he took loan of taka 1700.00. The said mortgage loan amount was not paid in time, for which the Manager of the said Bank sent the case to the Certificate Officer, Khulna Sadar, for starting Certificate Case No. 7/B.K.B/79- 80 for realisation of taka 9,593.00 in total including interest. The suit land was put to auction and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in open auction purchased the suit land and took delivery of possession on 30.10.1980. The defendants got their names mutated and they paid rent to the Government and since then the defendants had been possessing the suit land through Bargader. They also stated that neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessor got possession over the suit land. The plaintiffs claimed unspecified land on the basis of so-called sale certificate filed by the plaintiffs and, as such, the suit was liable to be dismissed.
